1 --- 2 title: Prefetching 3 description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js 4 --- 5 6 Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code. 7 8 This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it: 9 10 - [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work) 11 - [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically) 12 - [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching) 13 - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) 14 15 > **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path. 16 17 ## How does prefetching work? 18 19 When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route. 20 21 Next.js automatically splits your application into smaller JavaScript chunks based on routes. Instead of loading all the code upfront like traditional SPAs, only the code needed for the current route is loaded. This reduces the initial load time while other parts of the app are loaded in the background. By the time you click the link, the resources for the new route have already been loaded into the browser cache. 22 23 When navigating to the new page, there's no full page reload or browser loading spinner. Instead, Next.js performs a [client-side transition](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#client-side-transitions), making the page navigation feel instant. 24 25 ## What Next.js prefetches automatically 26 27 Next.js prefetches automatically in production. As each `` enters the viewport, Next.js prefetches the route behind it and schedules the work so a page full of links doesn't flood the network. How much of each route it prefetches depends on whether the route is static or dynamic, and changes when [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) is enabled. 28 29 ### Prefetching static vs. dynamic routes 30 31 Without Cache Components, a static route is prefetched in full, while a dynamic route is skipped unless it has a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) boundary. 32 33 | | **Static page** | **Dynamic page** | 34 | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 35 | **Prefetched** | Yes, full route | No, unless [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) | 36 | [**Client Cache TTL**](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) | 5 min (default) | Off, unless [enabled](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes) | 37 | **Server roundtrip on click** | No | Yes, streamed after [shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) | 38 39 > **Good to know:** During the initial navigation, the browser fetches the HTML, JavaScript, and React Server Components (RSC) Payload. For subsequent navigations, the browser will fetch the RSC Payload for Server Components and JS bundle for Client Components. 40 41 ### Automatic prefetch 42 43 ```tsx filename="app/ui/nav-link.tsx" switcher 44 import Link from 'next/link' 45 46 export default function NavLink() { 47 return About 48 } 49 ``` 50 51 ```jsx filename="app/ui/nav-link.js" switcher 52 import Link from 'next/link' 53 54 export default function NavLink() { 55 return About 56 } 57 ``` 58 59 | **Context** | **Prefetched payload** | **Client Cache TTL** | 60 | ----------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 61 | No `loading.js` | Entire page | 5 min ([`staleTimes.static`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) | 62 | With `loading.js` | Layout to first loading boundary | Off by default ([`staleTimes.dynamic`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) | 63 64 Automatic prefetching runs only in production. Disable with `prefetch={false}` or use the wrapper in [Disabled Prefetch](#disabled-prefetch). 65 66 ### Prefetch scheduling 67 68 Next.js maintains a small task queue, which prefetches in the following order: 69 70 1. Links in the viewport 71 2. Links showing user intent (hover or touch) 72 3. Newer links replace older ones 73 4. Links scrolled off-screen are discarded 74 75 The scheduler prioritizes likely navigations while minimizing unused downloads. 76 77 > **Good to know**: With the **experimental** [`useOffline`](/docs/app/guides/offline-support) config enabled, pending prefetches resume through this queue when the app recovers from a connectivity drop. 78 79 ### Client cache 80 81 Next.js stores prefetched React Server Component payloads in memory, keyed by route segments. When navigating between sibling routes (e.g. `/dashboard/settings` → `/dashboard/analytics`), Next.js reuses the parent layout and only fetches the updated leaf page. 82 83 ### Partial Prefetching 84 85 With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) enabled via the [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) config (which requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching)), prefetching switches from the all-or-nothing model above to a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): 86 87 - **One shell per route, shared across links.** `` prefetches the route's App Shell, which holds its static and session output. Any number of links to the same route reuse that one shell, fetched once as the first link enters the viewport, so a page with many links makes fewer prefetch requests than prefetching each route in full. 88 - **The rest streams in.** Uncached data streams in after navigation, behind the shell's `` boundaries. A link can also resolve its URL data (`searchParams`, `params`) at prefetch time with [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching). 89 - **Invalidations refresh prefetches.** Data invalidations (`revalidateTag`, `revalidatePath`) silently refresh associated prefetches. 90 91 See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the behavior change and the recommended adoption path. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) to resolve cached URL-specific content before navigation with `prefetch={true}`. 92 93 ## Controlling prefetching 94 95 Next.js prefetches with defaults you can tune per link when they don't fit your resource budget or navigation patterns. 96 97 ### Manual prefetch 98 99 To prefetch manually, import the `useRouter` hook from `next/navigation`, then call `router.prefetch()` to warm routes outside the viewport or in response to analytics, hover, or scroll. 100 101 ```tsx 102 'use client' 103 104 import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation' 105 import { CustomLink } from '@components/link' 106 107 export function PricingCard() { 108 const router = useRouter() 109 110 return ( 111
router.prefetch('/pricing')}> 112 {/* other UI elements */} 113 View Pricing 114
115 ) 116 } 117 ``` 118 119 To prefetch a URL when a component loads, see [Extending or ejecting link](#extending-or-ejecting-link). 120 121 ### Hover-triggered prefetch 122 123 > **Proceed with caution:** Extending `Link` opts you into maintaining prefetching, cache invalidation, and accessibility concerns. Do this only when the defaults are insufficient. 124 125 By default, `` prefetches when it enters the viewport. To prefetch only the links a user is likely to visit, defer prefetching until they hover over a link: 126 127 ```tsx 128 'use client' 129 130 import Link from 'next/link' 131 import { useState } from 'react' 132 133 export function HoverPrefetchLink({ 134 href, 135 children, 136 }: { 137 href: string 138 children: React.ReactNode 139 }) { 140 const [active, setActive] = useState(false) 141 142 return ( 143 setActive(true)} 147 > 148 {children} 149 150 ) 151 } 152 ``` 153 154 `prefetch={null}` restores default (static) prefetching once the user shows intent. 155 156 ### Extending or ejecting link 157 158 You can extend the `` component to create your own custom prefetching strategy. For example, using the [ForesightJS](https://foresightjs.com/docs/integrations/nextjs) library which prefetches links by predicting the direction of the user's cursor. 159 160 Alternatively, you can use [`useRouter`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router) to recreate some of the native `` behavior. However, be aware this opts you into maintaining prefetching and cache invalidation. 161 162 ```tsx 163 'use client' 164 165 import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation' 166 import { useEffect } from 'react' 167 168 function ManualPrefetchLink({ 169 href, 170 children, 171 }: { 172 href: string 173 children: React.ReactNode 174 }) { 175 const router = useRouter() 176 177 useEffect(() => { 178 let cancelled = false 179 const poll = () => { 180 if (!cancelled) router.prefetch(href, { onInvalidate: poll }) 181 } 182 poll() 183 return () => { 184 cancelled = true 185 } 186 }, [href, router]) 187 188 return ( 189 { 192 event.preventDefault() 193 router.push(href) 194 }} 195 > 196 {children} 197 198 ) 199 } 200 ``` 201 202 Next.js invokes [`onInvalidate`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router#userouter) when it suspects cached data is stale, so you can refresh the prefetch. 203 204 > **Good to know:** An `a` tag triggers a full page navigation. Use `onClick` to prevent it, then call `router.push` to navigate on the client. 205 206 ### Disabled prefetch 207 208 You can fully disable prefetching for certain routes for more fine-grained control over resource consumption. 209 210 ```tsx 211 'use client' 212 213 import Link, { LinkProps } from 'next/link' 214 215 function NoPrefetchLink({ 216 prefetch, 217 ...rest 218 }: LinkProps & { children: React.ReactNode }) { 219 return 220 } 221 ``` 222 223 For example, you may still want to have consistent usage of `` in your application, but links in your footer might not need to be prefetched when entering the viewport. 224 225 ## Troubleshooting 226 227 ### Triggering unwanted side-effects during prefetching 228 229 If your layouts or pages are not [pure](https://react.dev/learn/keeping-components-pure#purity-components-as-formulas) and have side-effects (e.g. tracking analytics), Next.js might run them when the route is prefetched, not when the user visits the page. 230 231 To avoid this, move side-effects to a `useEffect` hook or a Server Action triggered from a Client Component. 232 233 **Before**: 234 235 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher 236 import { trackPageView } from '@/lib/analytics' 237 238 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 239 // This runs during prefetch 240 trackPageView() 241 242 return
{children}
243 } 244 ``` 245 246 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher 247 import { trackPageView } from '@/lib/analytics' 248 249 export default function Layout({ children }) { 250 // This runs during prefetch 251 trackPageView() 252 253 return
{children}
254 } 255 ``` 256 257 **After**: 258 259 ```tsx filename="app/ui/analytics-tracker.tsx" switcher 260 'use client' 261 262 import { useEffect } from 'react' 263 import { trackPageView } from '@/lib/analytics' 264 265 export function AnalyticsTracker() { 266 useEffect(() => { 267 trackPageView() 268 }, []) 269 270 return null 271 } 272 ``` 273 274 ```jsx filename="app/ui/analytics-tracker.js" switcher 275 'use client' 276 277 import { useEffect } from 'react' 278 import { trackPageView } from '@/lib/analytics' 279 280 export function AnalyticsTracker() { 281 useEffect(() => { 282 trackPageView() 283 }, []) 284 285 return null 286 } 287 ``` 288 289 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher 290 import { AnalyticsTracker } from '@/app/ui/analytics-tracker' 291 292 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 293 return ( 294

Used as the default prefetch payload during client navigations, the loading state when a [per-link prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) is not ready, and the fallback for [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components).

17-# B
18-
19-## Build time
20-
21-The stage when your application is being compiled. During build time, Next.js transforms your code into optimized files for production, generates static pages, and prepares assets for deployment. See the [`next build` CLI reference](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-build-options).
22-
23-# C
24-
25-## Cache Components
26-
27-A feature that enables component and function-level caching using the [`"use cache"` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). Cache Components allows you to mix static, cached, and dynamic content within a single route by prerendering a static HTML shell that's served immediately, while dynamic content streams in when ready. Configure cache duration with [`cacheLife()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife), tag cached data with [`cacheTag()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag), and invalidate on-demand with [`updateTag()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag). Learn more in the [Cache Components guide](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
28-
--
165:A prefetching strategy for [Cache Components](#cache-components) routes where a `<Link>` prefetches a per-route [App Shell](#app-shell) by default instead of the full page. Enable it with [`partialPrefetching: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`. Learn more in the [Adopting Partial Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).
166-
167-## Partial Prerendering (PPR)
168-
169-A rendering optimization that combines prerendering and dynamic rendering in a single route. The static shell is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, providing the best of both rendering strategies. Learn more in [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
170-
171-## Prefetching
172-
173-Loading a route in the background before the user navigates to it. Next.js automatically prefetches routes linked with the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) when they enter the viewport, making navigation feel instant. Learn more in the [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching).
174-
175-## Prerendering
176-
177-When a component is rendered at [build time](#build-time) or in the background during [revalidation](#revalidation). The result is HTML and [RSC Payload](#rsc-payload), which can be cached and served from a CDN. Prerendering is the default for components that don't use [Request-time APIs](#request-time-apis).
178-
179-## Proxy
180-
--
278:Data that identifies a specific URL, such as the pathname and query parameters. In the App Router this means [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) and [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional), and the client hooks that read them like [`usePathname`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname) and [`useSearchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params). URL data varies per link, not per session, so it can't be part of a shared [App Shell](#app-shell).
279-
280-## `"use cache"` Directive
281-
282-A directive that marks a component or function as cacheable. It can be placed at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file are cacheable, or inline at the top of a function or component to mark that specific scope as cacheable. Learn more in the [`"use cache"` reference](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache).
283-
284-## `"use client"` Directive
285-
286-A special React directive that marks the boundary between server and client code. It must be placed at the top of a file, before any imports or other code. It indicates that React Components, helper functions, variable declarations, and all imported dependencies should be included in the [client bundle](#client-bundles). Learn more in the [`"use client"` reference](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-client).
287-
288-## `"use server"` Directive
289-
290-A directive that marks a function as a [Server Function](#server-function) that can be called from client-side code. It can be placed at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file are Server Functions, or inline at the top of a function to mark that specific function. Learn more in the [`"use server"` reference](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-server).

16	
17	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
18	
19	To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
20	
21	Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
22	
23	> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
24	
25	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
26	
27	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
28	
29	Install the skill:
30	
31	```bash filename="Terminal"
32	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
33	```
34	
35	Then give the agent this prompt:
36	
37	```prompt
38	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
39	```
40	
41	## Or adopt by hand
42	
43	To adopt an existing app by hand:
44	
45	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
46	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
47	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
48	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
49	5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
50	
51	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
52	
53	## Enable Partial Prefetching
54	
55	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
56	
57	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
58	
59	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
60	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
61	
62	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
63	  cacheComponents: true,
64	  partialPrefetching: true,
65	}
66	
67	export default nextConfig
68	```
69	
70	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
71	
72	## What changes for `<Link>`
73	
74	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
75	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
76	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
78	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
79	
80	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
81	
82	## Migrate existing full prefetches
83	
84	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
85	
86	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
87	
88	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
89	
90	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
91	
92	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same assertions after adopting the destination. A failure identifies UI the App Shell no longer carries, so you can cache the data or subtree that restores it. The passing test provides regression coverage.
93	
94	### Static or cached content
95	
96	The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:

101	// After
102	<Link href="/about">About</Link>
103	```

Shorter-lived content streams in after the navigation instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior).

153	### Session content
154	
155	Content behind [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) varies per session, not per link, and [session data resolves in the App Shell](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#include-session-data-in-the-shell), so cached session content still gets included. 245	### URL data
246	
247	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
248	
249	### Real-time content
250	
251	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
252	
253	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
254	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
255	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
256	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
257	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
258	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
259	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

261	## Adopting incrementally
262	
263	Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
264	
265	Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. 338	## Move URL data behind Suspense
339	
340	With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:

I made the changes and verified the build:

1. **`next.config.ts`** — added `partialPrefetching: true` alongside the existing `cacheComponents: true`, so `<Link>` prefetches a per-route App Shell instead of the full page.
2. **`app/page.tsx`** — added `prefetch={true}` to each project link, so cached content depending on the URL slug (the title) resolves ahead of the click.
3. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — split the page into two independent `<Suspense>` boundaries: `Title` (cached by slug, resolves during the per-link prefetch — so it's ready instantly on click) and `Details` (guarded by `await unstable_navigation()` before the cached lookup, which keeps it out of every prefetch stage and defers it to the actual navigation).

This is the pattern this fork's docs describe for exactly this case (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/.../functions/navigation.md`) — title/body prefetched, comments/details deferred via `unstable_navigation()`.

Verified `npm run build` succeeds, with `/projects/[slug]` reported as a Partial Prerender route, and a direct fetch of the page renders both the title and details correctly. I couldn't fully replicate the browser's segment-prefetch protocol via curl to see the prefetch payload directly (no browser available in this sandbox to confirm visually), but the implementation matches the documented API exactly and the full render is correct.
